headline: Workers block Dhaka-Sylhet highway to demand Ashuganj Fertilizer Factory restart
summary: Protesters claim the plant has been intentionally shut down for 1.5 years to facilitate the leasing of its land for private interests.
details: Workers and employees of the Ashuganj Fertilizer Factory blocked the Dhaka-Sylhet highway on Monday, demanding the immediate restart of the plant, which has been closed for approximately one and a half years.
The protest began around 9:30 AM with a human chain program organized by the factory's workers' union in front of the Syed Nazrul Islam Bridge toll plaza.
Following the human chain, the agitated workers blocked the highway for a period of time and held a protest rally.
The demonstration received solidarity support from top leaders of the Ashuganj Upazila BNP, Jamaat-e-Islami, National Nagarik Party, and their affiliated organizations.
CBA leaders from the Ashuganj Thermal Power Plant, as well as members of local CNG, truck, and rickshaw owners' associations, also joined the protest.
Speakers at the rally alleged that the national institution, which is highly profitable and farmer-friendly, has been plannedly shut down for 1.5 years.
They further claimed that there are deep conspiracies to lease out the factory's valuable land for private interests.

The protesters warned that if the factory is not reopened and the land-leasing conspiracy is stopped, they will launch more severe movements, including blocking all communications to the northern and eastern regions.
caption:
A major highway blocked as workers demand the restart of a fertilizer plant shut for 1.5 years.

Workers and employees of the Ashuganj Fertilizer Factory blocked the Dhaka-Sylhet highway on Monday, demanding the immediate restart of the plant, which has been closed for approximately one and a half years.

The protest began around 9:30 AM with a human chain program organized by the factory's workers' union in front of the Syed Nazrul Islam Bridge toll plaza.

Following the human chain, the agitated workers blocked the highway for a period of time and held a protest rally.

The demonstration received solidarity support from top leaders of the Ashuganj Upazila BNP, Jamaat-e-Islami, National Nagarik Party, and their affiliated organizations.

CBA leaders from the Ashuganj Thermal Power Plant, as well as members of local CNG, truck, and rickshaw owners' associations, also joined the protest.

Speakers at the rally alleged that the national institution, which is highly profitable and farmer-friendly, has been plannedly shut down for 1.5 years.

They further claimed that there are deep conspiracies to lease out the factory's valuable land for private interests.

The protesters warned that if the factory is not reopened and the land-leasing conspiracy is stopped, they will launch more severe movements, including blocking all communications to the northern and eastern regions.

headline: Fuel prices remain unchanged for September
summary: The government has decided to keep the retail prices of diesel, kerosene, octane, and petrol the same for the coming month.
details: The government has adjusted fuel prices for the market in September, keeping the rates unchanged. As a result, the latest retail prices for diesel, kerosene, octane, and petrol will remain in effect for this month.
Current prices are set at 115 BDT per liter for diesel, 135 BDT for kerosene, 145 BDT for octane, and 140 BDT for petrol.
A notification from the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources on Monday (August 31) confirmed the price coordination.
The notification stated that the prices determined on May 31 were approved by the appropriate authorities to be maintained for the month of September.
caption:
Fuel prices stay the same. No changes for diesel, petrol, and octane this September.

The government has adjusted fuel prices for the market in September, keeping the rates unchanged. As a result, the latest retail prices for diesel, kerosene, octane, and petrol will remain in effect for this month.

Current prices are set at 115 BDT per liter for diesel, 135 BDT for kerosene, 145 BDT for octane, and 140 BDT for petrol.

A notification from the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources on Monday (August 31) confirmed the price coordination.

The notification stated that the prices determined on May 31 were approved by the appropriate authorities to be maintained for the month of September.
